claims.text: Nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalysts exhibit high ethanol oxidation activity.
PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyzes ethanol oxidation through an atypical 12-electron process.
Intrinsic local electronic-structure heterogeneity controls the ethanol oxidation activity and selectivity of PtPdRhRuIrOs.
Random alloying in PtPdRhRuIrOs produces a Gaussian distribution of adsorption energies for ethanol and its intermediates.
Electronic heterogeneity creates complementary strongly binding and weakly binding active-site subsets.
Strongly binding sites promote ethanol adsorption, initial dehydrogenation, and C-C bond activation.
Weakly binding sites facilitate oxidation of later oxygenated intermediates and complete oxidation to CO2.
The initial PtPdRhRuIrOs nanoparticles are produced by rapid one-step chemical reduction and have a homogeneous random atomic distribution.
Inert-atmosphere thermal annealing will induce partial elemental segregation or chemical ordering in PtPdRhRuIrOs.
Annealing-induced segregation or ordering will reduce local electronic heterogeneity and narrow the spread of adsorption energies.
Neighboring sites with different local electronic structures can influence selectivity in complex reactions involving high-entropy alloys.
Cooperation between strongly and weakly binding neighboring sites lowers the barriers required for complete 12-electron ethanol oxidation.
Reducing electronic heterogeneity by annealing will diminish the cooperative dual-site effect.
The annealed catalyst will have lower ethanol oxidation activity than the disordered baseline.
Annealing will shift the product distribution away from CO2 and toward partial oxidation products such as acetaldehyde or acetic acid.
The proposed mechanism is expected to operate at 60-80 °C in typical acidic or alkaline ethanol-containing electrolytes.
The proposed mechanism may fail at extreme temperatures, very high current densities, or in the presence of strongly adsorbing species that substantially alter surface states.
If reduced heterogeneity produces similar or higher activity while retaining 12-electron selectivity, the proposed governing role of heterogeneity would be falsified.
